title: The plant's cell page: three groups, and it fits now
question: Are these the right three groups, and is STATE the right one to land on when you click a plant?
context_md:
The plant page was 302px tall on a 320px screen, and there was no clamp -- it
was being drawn at y = -42, so the title and the AT / MATERIAL / TEMPERATURE /
ORGANISM rows were off the top edge. It did not look cut off; it looked like a
page that starts at ENERGY.

The readout is now three named groups. LIFE is where the individual came from
and never changes. STATE is what moves while the box runs. GENOME is what it
was dealt at birth. An ant's gut bias and birth grant moved into GENOME on that
rule.

The fold is greedy rather than one-at-a-time: the group you last clicked is
served first, then the rest fill from the top with whatever still fits. So on a
plant you get LIFE and STATE open with "+ GENOME 11" shut (A); click GENOME and
it trades STATE for it (B). A shut group always says how many rows are behind
it, so nothing disappears silently.

An ant's page does not fold at all -- eight rows fit beside the cell block with
room to spare, so that page is exactly what it always was.

I built it as a true accordion first and it was worse: LIFE is three rows and
fits beside either eleven-row block with 14px left over, so closing it bought
nothing and took away the individual's identity while you were reading its
numbers.

Both images are the same plant, one click apart.

items.label: as it opens: LIFE + STATE, GENOME shut (11 rows behind it)
after clicking GENOME: it trades STATE for the genome
